label: input z in the first three original positions
explanation: Fires whenever the input token is the letter z at original positions 0, 1, or 2 (t <= 2), and essentially nowhere else: never on any other token, never on z at positions 4 and later, only rarely (167 steps) on z at t=3, and never on the delimiter or in the copy phase. Dev P=1.00, R=0.997. Magnitude depends on position: z at t=1 is strongest (up to 1.46, e.g. after j or q), z at t=0 sits around 0.66 of max, and z at t=2 around 0.6-0.7 of max. A repeated z (in_first=0) within the first three positions still fires. It is a token-identity detector restricted to early positions.

issues: Minor overstatement: 'never fires during the copy phase' and 'never on z at position 4 or later' are not quite true. The dev profile shows 2 copy-phase activations, both at t=5 with recall_idx=2, and they carry 0.000 of the activation mass. This is negligible noise.

All 152 test-split misses are z at t=3 with tiny activations (0.03-0.09 of max). Together they hold 0.0% of the activation mass, so this is a faint tail of the same pattern, not a separate case. There are 0 false positives.

Verified: 100% of activation mass is on in_tok z. Mass shares are t=0 0.286, t=1 0.421, t=2 0.294. The top activations are z at t=1 at 1.00 of max (for example after j), and z at t=0 or t=2 sits around 0.61-0.72 of max. Repeated z fires (j z z gives 1.00 then 0.68). Test results: precision 1.0, recall 0.997, F1 0.998, mass recall 0.9998.
